description: Alert design, alerting best practices, on-call management, and incident response for Java backend systems

questions.question: What makes a good alert and how do you avoid alert fatigue?
questions.answer: Good alert: 1) Actionable - requires human intervention, 2) Urgent - needs immediate attention, 3) Real - actual user impact, 4) Specific - clear what's wrong. Avoid alert fatigue: 1) Alert on symptoms not causes (user-facing issues not internal metrics), 2) Set appropriate thresholds (prevent false positives), 3) Use severity levels wisely, 4) Aggregate related alerts, 5) Regular review and tuning. Bad alert: 'CPU > 70%' (not necessarily user-facing). Good alert: 'Error rate > 1% for 5 minutes' (users affected). Example: Payment service CPU spikes to 90% but P99 latency still 300ms, users unaffected - don't page. Error rate jumps to 5%, page immediately. Alert runbook includes: what's wrong, user impact, initial investigation steps, escalation path. Review metrics: alerts per week, time to acknowledge, time to resolve, false positive rate. Target: <5 pages per week per person, <1% false positives.

questions.question: How do you implement multi-level alerting (warning, critical) with escalation in Prometheus Alertmanager?
questions.answer:
Multi-level alerting with Alertmanager routes alerts by severity, implements escalation.

Prometheus rules:
groups:
  - name: payment-alerts
    rules:
      # Warning - team Slack
      - alert: PaymentLatencyHigh
        expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="payment"}[5m])) > 0.5
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          service: payment
        annotations:
          summary: "Payment P99 latency > 500ms"
          description: "Current: {{ $value }}s"
      
      # Critical - page on-call
      - alert: PaymentServiceDown
        expr: up{job="payment"} == 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          service: payment
        annotations:
          summary: "Payment service is down"
          runbook: "https://wiki/runbooks/payment-down"
      
      - alert: PaymentErrorRateHigh
        expr: (rate(http_requests_total{job="payment",status=~"5.*"}[5m]) / rate(http_requests_total{job="payment"}[5m])) > 0.01
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          service: payment
        annotations:
          summary: "Payment error rate > 1%"

Alertmanager config:
route:
  receiver: default
  group_by: ['alertname', 'service']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  
  routes:
    # Warning alerts to Slack
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: slack-warnings
      continue: true
    
    # Critical alerts with escalation
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: pagerduty-primary
      repeat_interval: 5m
      routes:
        # Escalate if not acked in 10 min
        - match:
            severity: critical
          receiver: pagerduty-secondary
          group_wait: 10m

receivers:
  - name: slack-warnings
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/XXX'
        channel: '#alerts-warning'
        title: '{{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}'
        text: '{{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.summary }}\n{{ end }}'
  
  - name: pagerduty-primary
    pagerduty_configs:
      - service_key: 'primary-team-key'
        severity: '{{ .GroupLabels.severity }}'
        description: '{{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}: {{ .Annotations.summary }}'
  
  - name: pagerduty-secondary
    pagerduty_configs:
      - service_key: 'escalation-team-key'

Inhibition rules (suppress warnings when critical):
inhibit_rules:
  - source_match:
      severity: critical
    target_match:
      severity: warning
    equal: ['service']

Escalation: Critical alert → PagerDuty primary → If not acked in 10 min → PagerDuty secondary → If not resolved in 30 min → Escalate to manager.
